phase_obstruction_criterion.value_or_interval: f = A L(s,chi) + conj(A) L(s,conj chi) with A = (1 - i kappa)/2 and chi the odd primitive character mod 5, so for Re s > 1 a zero of f is equivalent to arg L(s,chi)/L(s,conj chi) = pi + 2 arctan(kappa) mod 2 pi; each prime p = 2,3 mod 5 contributes a factor (1+u)/(1-u) with |u| = p^{-sigma}, whose argument is at most 2 arctan(p^{-sigma}); hence Theta(sigma) < tau implies no zero on Re s = sigma, and Theta decreasing closes the half-plane
phase_obstruction_criterion.frame: frame-free (a statement in the s plane)
phase_obstruction_criterion.grade_detail: exact elementary analysis on top of decided constants. Uses the Euler products of two Dirichlet L-functions on Re s > 1 (absolutely convergent, nonvanishing), one Moebius image of a disc, F entire with F(s) = F(1-s), and the classical nonvanishing of Gamma with poles only at s = -1,-3,.... No Bohr theory, no Kronecker theorem, no Euler product for f itself, which has none. The character decomposition a_n = A chi(n) + conj(A) conj(chi)(n) is decided as five acb residual balls containing 0 with radius below 1e-40, chi taken from flint's Dirichlet character table. Because C^2 - rho^2 = 1 for the Moebius image disc, the argument-maximising point has modulus exactly 1, so the |R| = 1 constraint is free and no modulus-phase trade sharpens this further
phase_obstruction_criterion.backend: python-flint 0.9.0 (Arb) for the decided constants; mpmath dps 30-40 for the measured confirmations

phase_tail_closed_by_euler_product.value_or_interval: the tail of Theta beyond the sieve limit is closed by the Euler products of zeta and L(.,chi5) themselves: T1 - Tchi = 2 Q + (E_chi - E_1) with every even-k term cancelling exactly (chi5(p)^2 = 1 for p > P >= 5), leaving |E_chi - E_1| <= eps3 = (2/3) P^{1-3 sigma}/((3 sigma - 1)(1 - P^{-2 sigma}))
phase_tail_closed_by_euler_product.grade_detail: no explicit pi(x) estimate, no Chebyshev bound and no cited prime-counting inequality enters anywhere. The even-k cancellation is what makes this sharp: bounding E_chi and E_1 separately leaves an O(P^{1-2 sigma}) error, which at P = 1e5 and sigma = 1.12036249819 is 2.52e-07 against 4.42e-13, a factor 5.7e+05
phase_tail_closed_by_euler_product.backend: python-flint 0.9.0 (Arb); mpmath.iv leg uses Euler-Maclaurin over arithmetic progressions and an alternating-series bracket for arctan

block_route_decided_and_useless.grade: decided, and decided to be useless for a half-plane
block_route_decided_and_useless.grade_detail: regrouping into period-5 blocks and applying the mean value theorem gives |B_k| <= |s|[3(5k+1)^{-sigma-1} + kappa(5k+2)^{-sigma-1}], which is O(n^{-sigma-1}) per block instead of O(n^{-sigma}) per term but carries |s| = sqrt(sigma^2 + t^2). The |s| is not an artifact: both pairs in a period share the midpoint 5k+5/2 and their first-order terms add, B_k = s(3+kappa)(5k+5/2)^{-s-1}(1 + O(|s|/n)), so a trapezoid correction only refines the constant and the next order carries |s|^2. Measured, the bound tracks |B_k| to 1.0062 when |s| << n and overshoots by 1104 when |s| >> n. de Bruijn Theorem 13 consumes a half-plane statement, which this cannot give; beyond T = 10 it is already worse than the phase bound. Recorded because it is the natural thing to try
